description:
FOUND s494 (Fable, 2026-09-21) while writing the #2092 probe file -- its first comment line said "NO `use utf8`" and the labels came out corrupted.  ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s494/d2092/t-*.pl, perl 5.40.3 vs main 863d3e20:
    # this file does not use utf8;
    print "lit é\n";                 perl: 6c 69 74 20 c3 a9 0a        pcl: 6c 69 74 20 e9 0a
  same with `my $s = "use utf8;";`, with a POD block containing `  use utf8;`, and with `use utf8;` after `__END__`.  NOT triggered by `utf8::decode(...)`, `use feature "unicode_strings"`, `use v5.12` (probed: those leave the bytes alone, as perl does).
MECHANISM (read): Pl/Parser.pm `_maybe_decode_utf8`, line 199: `return $src unless defined $src && $src =~ /\buse\s+utf8\b/;` -- a regex over the RAW SOURCE, before PPI sees it (the decode has to happen before the parse, which is why it is textual).
REACH, measured: in lib/ + cpan-tests/ ONE .pm mentions `use utf8` only outside code (Test::More's POD) and it has no high bytes -- so nothing on disk is hit today; the carrier to worry about is a USER's module whose POD shows `use utf8;` in its synopsis while the module itself holds Latin-1 / UTF-8 bytes in literals without the pragma.
FIX SHAPE: keep the pre-parse scan, make it read CODE only -- skip POD (`^=[a-zA-Z]` ... `^=cut`), everything from `^__END__` / `^__DATA__`, full-line and trailing `#` comments are the hard part without a lexer, so: require the STATEMENT shape at the start of a logical line (`^\s*use\s+utf8\s*;` or after `;` / `{`) and accept that a heredoc body or a multi-line string containing such a line still fools it (say so in the comment).  If a cheap exact answer is wanted instead: PPI parses BYTES fine and `use utf8` is ASCII, so parse first, ask the tree for a PPI::Statement::Include named utf8, and re-parse decoded only when it is there -- a double parse for `use utf8` files only; MEASURE it against the 50 % compile budget before choosing.  perl's pragma is LEXICAL (`{ use utf8; ... }` decodes that block only, `no utf8` ends it) -- file-wide is the standing approximation (docs/not-supported.md Unicode section); do not widen this task into that.
ALSO CHECK the sibling: the runtime's module loader / `do FILE` / `require` path decides decoding too (#1084: `p-do` and `_maybe_decode_utf8` were two halves) -- grep for a second textual test (feedback_check_for_a_second_copy).
BAR: the four probes = perl; Pl/t/utf8-source-01.t gains the four rows + a positive row that a REAL `use utf8;` after a comment line still decodes; corpus-diff IDENTICAL expected (measured: no on-disk file is hit); gate.  No gen bump if corpus-diff is identical.
SIZE: filler, under an hour.

=== DONE (s494u) ===
Pl::Parser::_source_says_use_utf8 replaces the /\buse\s+utf8\b/ test in _maybe_decode_utf8: a CODE-only textual scan (POD blocks and everything after __END__/__DATA__ skipped, full-line # comments skipped, a trailing ` # ...` cut) that requires the STATEMENT shape (line start, or after `;` / `{`).  Still fooled, knowingly, by a heredoc body / multi-line string holding such a line (said in the comment).  No second textual copy exists (grep: the runtime's do/require go through the same function, #1084).  All ten ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s494/d2092/t-*.pl probes = perl.  Guard Pl/t/utf8-source-01.t rows 42-46 (42-45 fail on a 209e7533 extraction; 46 = a real `use strict; use utf8;` after a comment still decodes).  corpus-diff: no file moved by this commit (lc.t is #2092's).  Commit "s494u #2192: `use utf8` is found as a STATEMENT in CODE" on the s494u branch (sha changes at each rebase; 4dcf392b before the s501 rebase).
subject: SILENT WRONG (cheap): `use utf8` is detected TEXTUALLY -- a COMMENT, a POD block (a SYNOPSIS that says `use utf8;`), a string, or text after `__END__` that merely MENTIONS "use utf8" makes PCL decode the WHOLE source file, so a literal's UTF-8 bytes C3 A9 become the one character U+00E9 and are printed as the single byte E9 (invalid UTF-8 on the user's terminal)
